clue.text: Broken promise leads to religious schism

definitions.meaning: a betrayal of trust or a pledge not kept
a split in a church, read literally as a rupture in a creed

explanation.surface: A betrayed pledge sets off a split in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' is only a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a betrayal of trust and, read literally, a rupture in someone's religious creed.

parts.note: read as smoking things that are also jackets: a short double-breasted sailor's coat shares its name with slang for cannabis cigarettes

explanation.surface: A question about the velvet coats worn for an after-dinner cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the gentleman's lounging coat; instead the word names both a sailor's jacket and a hand-rolled joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a type of short naval coat and also slang for marijuana cigarettes, which are smoked.

clue.text: Help to put on a Verdi opera

indicators.note: one piece is placed on top of the other in this down clue, so the first goes before the second

parts.note: help means aid

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to assist in staging an opera by Verdi.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of Verdi's 1871 opera about an Ethiopian princess.

clue.text: One who'd turned out for a dance

indicators.note: turned out suggests something rearranged and reshaped, so the letters of the words before it are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone who showed up to attend a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like 'attended', but it signals an anagram of ONEWHOD; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lively American country square-dance or the party where one is held.

indicators.note: concealing means one word hides the other inside it

parts.note: a charge is a fee
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Someone expects a price to be levied for hiding mineral deposits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' reads as an accusation in the surface but is a price; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to predict or see it coming in advance.

definitions.meaning: the book of the New Testament that comes just before the Epistle to the Romans

explanation.surface: Laws that the people of ancient Rome obeyed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, the Acts of the Apostles is immediately followed by Paul's Epistle to the Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes passed by parliament bear this name, as does the New Testament book preceding the Epistle to the Romans.

clue.text: It's flipping brown in charge — what a disaster!

indicators.note: flipping means the little word before it is turned over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation about a tanned person put in command who proves a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word, but it turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The liner that sank in 1912 has become a byword for any colossal catastrophe.

parts.note: the musician picture hides a lone animal that trumpets and has strayed from its herd

explanation.surface: A trumpet player walks out of his group to go solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a musical group but means a herd; the trumpeter is a large animal living alone and often dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangerous bull from the herd of tuskers that lives apart and trumpets alone fits the description.

clue.text: One gets down to the cleaning with this

definitions.text: One gets down to the cleaning with this

parts.words: One gets down to the cleaning with this
parts.note: down is soft plumage, so this cleaning tool is literally made of it

explanation.surface: A tool for someone who knuckles down to the housework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets down to' reads as 'starts on', but 'down' is the soft plumage the implement is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick tufted with plumes for flicking dirt off shelves is a household cleaning tool.

clue.text: Completed fitting but not yet paid

parts.note: something completed is over
fitting means due, as in due respect

explanation.surface: A tailor's fitting is finished but the bill remains unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitting' looks like a tailoring session but is an adjective meaning proper; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill past its payment date is late and still owing.

parts.note: call means to name, so to call again is to give a new name; the surface is a shopkeeper's farewell

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper urging a customer to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' reads as 'visit', but here it means name something.
explanation.definitionFit: To rename a book or film is to give it a fresh heading.

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter from the States was exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exploited has been manipulated for another's benefit.

parts.note: liner reads as a ship but means what lines or borders the sea

explanation.surface: A question about a big passenger ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liner' suggests a passenger ship, but it means the line the sea runs along.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore is the strip of land that edges the sea.

definitions.meaning: a pooled investment fund, called by this name in Britain, in which savers buy shares

explanation.surface: A remark on one way of trusting.
explanation.walkthrough: A UK investment fund divided into equal shares is called a ___ trust.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a single entity and also the British investment fund divided into shares.

parts.note: banks reads as financial institutions but means riverbanks, and the transfer is carrying people across water

explanation.surface: A money transfer from one bank to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests finance; here they are the sides of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat carrying passengers across a river moves them from one shore to the other.

clue.text: Clear evidence that the compositor's done his job

definitions.text: that the compositor's done his job
definitions.meaning: a trial print of typeset pages, checked before the final run

explanation.surface: Evidence that the typesetter has finished his work.
explanation.walkthrough: A compositor sets type; the trial impression he produces for checking has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means conclusive demonstration and also a trial print of typeset text for correction.

indicators.note: disposition can mean arrangement, so the letters of the neighbouring word are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia with a serious temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' reads as 'temperament' but means arrangement; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and this adjective both describe things from the lands of Asia.

clue.text: Some wear a cheerful smile in affliction

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people keep a happy face while suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smile in affliction' looks like a phrase about bravery; it is the definition, a pun on 'ear' in 'smile'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in the auditory organ is an affliction, and 'smile' contains the word for that organ in sound.

clue.text: Prepare to fight and pull out grenade

indicators.note: to pull something out of shape is to rearrange it, so the letters of grenade are reordered

explanation.surface: A soldier readies for battle by pulling the pin on a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pull out' evokes pulling a grenade's pin, but it signals an anagram; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencer's call, from French, warns an opponent to take a defensive stance before a bout.

clue.text: Recover and make an impression on an audience

definitions.meaning: to recuperate from an illness or setback

definitions.text: make an impression on an audience
definitions.meaning: to communicate a message successfully to listeners

explanation.surface: A performer gets better and wins over the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is like 'get across': a message that is understood by listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both recuperate and successfully put a point across to listeners.

clue.text: Watch the dance in which one has a pupil

parts.words: in which one has a pupil
parts.note: the pupil is the dark centre of the organ of sight
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Observe the dance where someone brings a student along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a student at a dance; it is part of the eye. The pieces go in answer order, the reverse of the clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare at someone closely is to watch them intently.

parts.note: a prop that stands at one side of a shelf row to keep volumes upright

explanation.surface: Biased backing for some branch of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-sided' suggests bias, but means the prop stands at one side of a row of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighted stand placed at the side of a row of volumes stops them toppling.

clue.text: Rod gets profit — cheap at the price

parts.note: a bar is a rod of metal
profit means gain

explanation.surface: A fisherman's rod is a good-value purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth more than its cost is a good deal for the shopper.

parts.note: an em is a printing measure of width
the Bar is the body of barristers
to proceed is to go

explanation.surface: A new measure from the legal profession moves towards a prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. An em is a typesetter's unit of width.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition on trade with a country is a form of ban.

definitions.meaning: popular records or successes, the question mark showing a loose example

explanation.surface: Critics savaging the top-selling books.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means blows and also chart-topping successes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means strikes and also popular successes such as chart-topping records.

clue.text: They need the will to succeed

definitions.text: They need the will to succeed

parts.words: They need the will to succeed
parts.note: will reads as determination but means a testament, and succeed means inherit

explanation.surface: A motivational line about people needing determination to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' reads as willpower, but it is the document naming beneficiaries; 'succeed' means take over an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Inheritors depend on a testament to take over an estate.

parts.note: read as a tide running back out to sea

explanation.surface: A tap or reservoir goes dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs out of' suggests exhausting supply; read it as flowing back out, as the tide does.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide flows away from the shore, which is how the sea recedes.

clue.text: Aircraft control in a state of panic

definitions.meaning: a hinged section on an aeroplane wing

explanation.surface: Air traffic control is in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a hinged wing surface on a plane and also a fluster.

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: People living in poverty on marshy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A South African word for a shallow marsh or wetland; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa the term names a shallow, seasonally flooded hollow or marshy ground.

clue.text: Short story new to the French

parts.note: novel means new
la is French for the

explanation.surface: A brief tale that is a new thing to the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a prose work longer than a tale but shorter than a full book.

definitions.meaning: as a whole, as in the public in general

explanation.surface: A military commander has escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an officer but is an adjective, as in 'society at large'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a whole, as in the population generally, and also free or escaped.

definitions.note: describes a device that may be hooked on to another ship or a wall

parts.note: wrestling means grappling
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Someone may be addicted to a wrestling society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooked on' suggests addiction; the definition describes a grapnel that catches on to things.
explanation.definitionFit: The grapnel is a multi-pronged hook thrown to catch on to a ship or wall.
